utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Lazarevic. Judge Kamenova will not be with us today. She is absent on another official business. We have decided that the appropriate course in the interests of justice to is continue in her absence, so we shall continue with the cross-examination by Mr. Hannis. Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Good morning, General. Yesterday --

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you. Yesterday we talked about the Joint Command order in Exhibit P1966 and your amendment in P1967. And related to that, I'd like you to have a look at Exhibit P2014. And while we're waiting for that to come up, I'll tell you this is a 25th of May, 1999 document and it has that Pristina Corps numbering system. This is 455-262. It's an order to crush the Siptar terrorist forces in the Mount Drenica sector. Are you familiar with this document, General? Have you seen this before?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have. As part of the proofing with the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And I think we'll get -- we'll show you the last page in a minute. But while we've got this first page up, I've got a few questions for you. I see at the top above the "Order," it says: "To command of the MUP." Do you know who wrote that on there?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have firsthand knowledge. I can only suppose it is one of the operations officers in charge of distributing official documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. And I had a question for you about that -- that strictly confidential number 455-262. I know we've related that number 455 to the Pristina Corps, but we've seen other documents coming out of the Pristina Corps that -- that have a different number. Does "455" refer to some specific theme or topic regarding the Pristina Corps? Can you explain that to us?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the command of the Pristina Corps, as is the rule according to the rules of official correspondence in the Army of Yugoslavia, there are several reference numbers by organ within the command of the corps, by topic. There could have been several sub-numbers. The mobilisation organ would have their reference number. The security organ would have its own number. And that facilitated later archiving and handling. This correspondence beginning with "455" concerns the person processing the documents within the organ of the Pristina Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I'm not sure I understand what you mean by "455 concerns the person processing the documents." My question is: The "455," we've seen -- we've seen the document that was the first in this series in 1999. It -- that was 455-1, which is Exhibit P280 -- I see Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, it seems that this was not interpreted correctly. This number does not refer to the person processing the document but the organ processing the document. That's not one person but part of the command that processes the document. But you can ask this again of General Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes. General, I had understood that that number referred to some -- some theme or some subject matter, rather than to a person or a -- an organ. I understand it relates to the Pristina Corps, that -- if you saw a document beginning with that number "455" in 1999, you would know it related or came from the Pristina Corps; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the Pristina Corps. But more specifically, from the operations organ of the Pristina Corps Command. That was a group of people, an organisational unit within the corps command.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. So then do all documents that come from -- in 1999, do all documents that came from the Pristina Corps operations organ have that number 455 on them, no matter what subject they're talking about?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: That, I think, must be fairly obvious, since you know where 455-1 is. -- If -- if we've got 455-1 in this case, then everything from the Pristina Corps operations organ can't be 455. I -- I wonder -- we don't really need to know how the whole system works, Mr. Lazarevic. We just need you to tell us what's the significance of "455."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There's no formal significance in it. There is a so-called -- there are so-called lists of documents by specific subject. One list of documents concerning the security of the border, bearing the number 150; a list of documents concerning the training of the reserve force, with a number 130; and so on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: That's not what we need to know. What we need to know what this relates to, with the number of 455. Don't go around the circle of telling us all the other numbers documents and what they mean. Tell us what this one means.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I cannot answer you specifically.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... So --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Various activities --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Is it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is not to me, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: What does it mean to you, then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It means to me that certain documents issued in the operations organ are logged in this list of documents bearing the initial number 455. The content dealt with under this number is different, varies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Back to you, Mr. Hannis. I'm none the wiser.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, I am -- I'm none the wiser either yet, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: If we could look at P2808 for a moment. And, General, this will be the -- the first document, -- as I understand it, this will be the first document in 1999 issued under the number 455; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. And 455, looking to that number, that indicates to you that this was written or came out of the operations organ of the Pristina Corps Command; correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And many of the documents in this series 455 do seem to relate to actions regarding breaking up and destroying Siptar terrorist forces. But -- but not all of them seem directly on that point. Can -- can you explain to me, is 455 related to a subject matter and the operations organ? It's those two things together that -- that make up 455?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That number primarily relates to the operations organ, but within the number 455 there may be different topics dealt with.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Do you know what topics were dealt with under 455 in 1999, other than operations against the Siptar terrorists or actions against the Siptar terrorists?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I remember, my Defence has tendered a part of these documents. And if I try to focus now and to be precise, there are documents that also relate to how one should act in executing tasks, although not direct execution of combat tasks; dislocation of troop and materiel reserves. There were a number of topics under this number 455.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Was there any other number related to the operations organ other than 455? Do you --

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: -- know what numbers those were?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At this moment, I cannot give you an answer, but the next time I have a chance I will have researched this and I would be able to give you and the Trial Chamber some other numbers. I know for a fact that there are other numbers, but I cannot tell you which at this moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Now, if we could go back to P2014. At this time, in May, the 25th of May, to your knowledge and understanding, to whom would this document have been directed if it says "the command of the MUP"? What individual would that refer to in this context at this time?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would appreciate it if we could see the last page of this document, because on that page it is clearly indicated to whom it was sent, and it is probably typed as well, not just handwritten.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: General, I can have the usher hand you a hard copy as well. I see the last page is up on the screen now too. And from my English, it looks like we just have your -- your name and your signature but we don't have any transmittal information.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, regrettably -- or rather, simply it's not written here. Usually on the left-hand side you can see the addressees. But let me get back to the first part of the question, because we are not assisted by this last page. This reference to "the command," that is in keeping with our combat rules, this -- this word. Not only the command of the MUP. It is addressed to the command of such-and-such a military unit. But here "MUP" is the acronym for the Ministry of the Interior but it is certainly not to the MUP in Belgrade. I believe it's very likely that it was sent either to one of the detachments involved in this action or perhaps the staff of the MUP in Pristina. Those are the two possibilities. I can now try to analyse this document, and I see that in -- under the heading "Tasks of units," this task should have involved a detachment of the MUP that is not yet defined at the moment of writing of this document. Other units of the MUP were not supposed to take part in this action. So I cannot really be very precise about this. I cannot know to whom precisely it was sent.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Well, let me ask you this: In item 5.1, it says: "The 252nd Armoured Brigade with the PJP Detachment and the JSO ..." Now, my understanding is that the PJP was a part of the -- the public security sector or public security side of the MUP; correct? Is that your understanding as well?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And my understanding also -- further is that the JSO was under the state security side of the MUP; correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: So if both sides of the house are going to be involved, does that help you in reaching any conclusion about who in the MUP this would have gone to if it's going to involve both sides, both public security and state security in an action in Kosovo in May of 1999?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, really based on this acronym, which is not adequate - it doesn't say "staff of the MUP"; it says just "MUP" - I can only be certain that it was not sent to the Ministry of the Interior in Belgrade. I would say that it was sent -- but I don't see it's indicated clearly to which detachment. It's probably to the staff of the MUP in Pristina. Or another possibility, if in the meantime the sender found out which detachment of the MUP, it could have been sent to the state security sector or the public security sector accordingly. This does not really explain.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Who would be the sender of this document? Who would be responsible for sending it to the command of the MUP?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: One of the operations officers from the command of the Pristina Corps, the so-called liaison officer, whose job it was to get in touch with and find this unit, to establish communication and to deliver this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I apologise. Just one second, sorry. Your Honour, I think we need to correct the transcript, because General Lazarevic said, page 8, line 13, "Those are all my assumptions." And we don't have it in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: General, you -- you were the author of this order. Do you recall anybody from your -- from your subordinates who would have been responsible for this, getting back to you and saying, "General, I don't know who I'm supposed to send this to," because it doesn't appear to be crystal clear as written. Do you recall any discussion about that?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall, but I hope that there will be a specific answer to this question as well soon, because I believe -- I hope a Defence witness, one of the future Defence witnesses will be the person who was directly charged with distributing documents towards units of the corps and specific detachments and compositions of the MUP who were involved in the action. At this moment, I don't even know who it would be, but I hope the person would come to testify.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: You don't know the name of who that person would be?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I know. I know. It's General Stefanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And he's --

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Radojko Stefanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And we've seen his name on your witness list. That's the same one; right?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct. Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I asked you if there's any significance to the fact that this order is dated the 25th of May, because recall that on the 24th of May you wrote your report about the non-subordination or the failure of MUP to be subordinated to the VJ; correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it makes sense. I did report that, but I did not get from my superior command -- commander an annulled order, an order that was cancelled. Instead, the order remained in force that MUP forces were re-subordinated to the army, and I simply couldn't do otherwise. As we see from one of these documents we saw a day or two ago when the Defence of General Lukic showed a number of these documents, and one of them was of this nature.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And the 25th of May was the date that's on General Pavkovic's report to the Supreme Command Staff about the non-subordination of MUP; correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I -- I don't recall. Was this -- was this an unusual occasion, or do you recall a number of other orders where at the top you wrote or someone typed this "to" -- "to the MUP," or to anybody in the MUP? Because most of the time we see those addresses referred to at the end of such documents; correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but this is not counter to the rules. I would say that it is in keeping with the rules when orders are concerned. Above the word "command" or "order," there should be a reference to the command. This must have been an officer who was particularly diligent in applying these rules. It is the customary way to write above the word "Order," "to the command," and then below you don't find the list of addressees. Instead, on every copy you find the words "to the command" this, "to the command" that, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. I understand. Item number 2 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Does that mean that this is the -- is a particular copy that was destined for the MUP and there will be others which have a different command at the top? For example, the command of the 252nd Armoured Brigade?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Precisely, Your Honour. Precisely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Now, did -- is it your Defence that -- oh, no, it's the Prosecution that have produced this document. Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: General, under item number 2, which I think is on the page in e-court, but you've also got the hard copy, "The task of the Pristina Corps." This is to block and crush the remaining Siptar terrorist forces. And in the last paragraph under "task," it says: "The command post shall be in the sector of the Pristina Corps Command premises in Pristina." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And right above that, the sentence before, it says: "Engage armed non-Siptar civilians to secure vital facilities and communications and protect and defend the local population." Now, in this context, who are those armed non-Siptar civilians? I know we've talked about it before, but I -- I guess I'm still not clear on it. Is this -- is this civil defence?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is civil defence. And this task of the Pristina Corps dates back to the month of February, based on the order defined by the army command, and that task of the corps cannot be changed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Now, I don't see any language here indicating or -- or directing anyone to coordinate with the Ministry of Defence for this engagement of the non-Siptar civilians. So did the VJ -- did the VJ have the authority to direct civil defence in these kinds of tasks?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. And I would like to draw the attention of the Trial Chamber to paragraph 4 - that's my decision - which does not mention that task at all. Paragraph 5, when I am issuing task, not a single unit gets that task. This is simply at the level of a general possible task that the corps received as part of prior orders and plans for use, even before the war, and that section is not changed. It is copied. If a specific order comes from the superior command or the Ministry of Defence for coordination and cooperation, then that would be defined.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. I guess that's a fair point. At this time I think we have some other orders where there are specific task for the non-Siptar population in the -- in the task for specific VJ units, but we'll look at those later. But I want to continue on about the use of this term "armed non-Siptar civilians" here. Are you saying this only refers to civil defence? Or does it also include civil protection?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that segment, this structure in the Ministry of Defence, primarily when one sees a task of this kind, it refers to the civil defence. But also the civilian protection is engaged in protection of the population. And as you can see in the last sentence here, primarily this refers to guards, patrols, units of the civil defence within the framework of the Ministry of Defence, but the civilian protection as part of this system may also be engaged to protect the civilian population and facilities or buildings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: What sentence is that? Can you help, Mr. Hannis?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: The sentence about armed non-Siptar civilians?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: No, no, the -- it says: "In the last sentence, this refers to guards, patrols, units of the civil defence within the framework of the Ministry of Defence."

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: That's not in this document, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Lazarevic, again, it may be translation, but you've just said: "As you can see in the last sentence here, this refers to guards, patrols, units of the civil defence." In which sentence are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the Prosecutor asked me whether the armed non-Siptar population refers to the civil defence, and I said "yes," and then I explained what the civil defence encompasses: Guards, patrols, and units of the civil defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, if I may assist so that we might expedite matters, I know what the witness is referring to. It was in another context. The last sentence before item 3, before the words "the command post shall be in the sector of the Pristina Corps Command premises in Pristina," above that it says: "Engage armed non-Siptar civilians to secure vital facilities and communications, and protect and defend the local population." That's what he was referring to. That was the context in which he said, "Look at the last sentence."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac, I appreciate your desire to help, but you've done the very opposite. It's not for you to give evidence here. It's for the witness to explain what his answers mean. He should be indeed more capable than you of explaining clearly what the document says and what his -- he was referring to. And I -- we can move on to something else now.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I do apologise. It was not my intention. You can listen to the tape and you will hear that that was the context in which it was said. I ask that the tape be reviewed. It was not my intention to put words in the witness's mouth that he did not say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Very well. We shall obtain a further check of -- of the interpretation of that passage. Thank you. Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And, General, what I -- what I'm trying to find out is that in -- in these orders where there's a reference to "the armed non-Siptar civilians," are you referring only to civil defence? Can you say "yes" or "no" to that one?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. So does it -- does it also include civil protection personnel?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Just one moment Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Sorry, Mr. Hannis. It was just a matter I thought that the other Judges should be aware of. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: So besides civil defence and civil protection, did it also include elements or units of something that we've heard some reference to during this case of -- of another group that was called local defence? Do you know what I'm referring to?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know what you're referring to.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, I seem to recall -- perhaps I'm looking ahead to a witness that is on your Defence team's list, of an individual who is from a village near Djakovica who is forecast as going to testify about the local defence in the village. And this is not civil protection and this is not civil defence. This is -- this is almost like a local police force, if you will, non-official MUP. You've never heard of any group like that in Kosovo in 1999?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, now you've put your question in more precise terms. What I know is that as early as 1998 the organs of local self-management organised local security, not local defence, not local police. At least, that's how I understood it. And that was what I knew at the time. It was local security. The local, mainly Albanian, population was involved in several villages and municipalities.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. But they would not be part of the armed non-Siptar civilians; correct? Because they're Siptars.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they were not all Siptars, to the best of my knowledge. This structure, so to speak, does not belong to the Ministry of Defence but to the local self-management, self-government authorities. They are not part of the civilian protection or civil defence and they do not belong to the category we are discussing, that is, the armed non-Siptar population.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: What about local security in Serb villages made up of non-Siptars? Wouldn't they be part of the non-Siptar civilians, the armed non-Siptar civilians?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I repeat that this is a very specific, conditionally speaking, institution. In some places where villages were purely Albanian, these were Albanians. Where they were mixed, the composition would be mixed. The weapons they had, as far as I can recall, were pistols, that is, side-arms. They carried side-arms. And their task was to restore confidence in Kosovo, inter-ethnic confidence at the level of the local communes and local self-government units. It was not connected to what you are asking me about. That was not it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. General, if I may say so, I -- I think I've actually heard witnesses here in court say it, if -- if not just in proofing with General Vasiljevic, that there have been comments about the orders written by you and they're complimentary comments. They hold this -- hold up your -- your orders as examples of -- of really well-written military document. And so if I may say, I -- it seems to me that you are a bit of a stickler for precision. Would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Every officer does his best, given the conditions, because some orders have to be written on one -- on one's knees because there's no desk. But every officer does his best to comply with the procedure and the rules. Whether I succeeded in this or not in the course of the war, I don't know, but everybody in the corps, including myself, did their best to do things properly and in the spirit of the rules.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, I think you're -- you're being too modest, General. We have had other witnesses testify about orders and documents drafted by other generals, and those documents were criticised. But I haven't heard that about yours. The point I want to make is that if "armed non-Siptar civilians" means only civil defence and civil protection, then why wouldn't you just say that, "engage the civil protection and civil defence units to secure vital facilities and communications and protect and defend the local population"? Wouldn't that have been more precise and clear for everyone to know what was meant?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: By Their Honours' leave, I wish to assist myself and Their Honours and to be very precise. I confess that your question is quite correct. I want to say that this term came into existence before the war when the civil protection and civil defence had not yet been mobilised. So that is the term, I repeat once more, which then seeped into the official documents of the corps as part of the task. And once it was defined in these terms and there were no specific tasks assigned, the operative officer in the corps command simply copied the clause from one document to another. If Their Honours can follow, the decisions and tasks are what mattered and nowhere in a decision of mine, either in this one or others, or in the tasks, can you see a structure bearing this name mentioned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Were there absolutely no Albanians in the civil defence or civil protection?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't -- I know hardly a single Serb who was among those 10.000 or so. I don't know. I really don't know what the ethnic composition of the civil protection and civil defence was. If you ask me now to say who was a Serb or something else, I wouldn't be able to tell you. I believe there were. There were even Albanians in the army units and members of other ethnic groups. I know that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: General, I don't recall if it was yesterday or not, but we were talking about some of these documents entitled "Joint Command" orders relating to actions against the Siptar terrorist forces. And you'll recall that phrase at the end on most of those that says something along the order of "all forces will be under the command and control of the Joint Command for Kosovo and Metohija." And you pointed out in one of your answers to Judge Bonomy, I think it was that, that meant -- that only referred to VJ forces, because this was a -- this was a 455-series document, which you have indicated to us means it's from the Pristina Corps. Do you recall that? Is that correct? That's your position that in those documents it was only referring to command and control of VJ units, not MUP?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I recall those documents with tasks relating exclusively to units of the army, that is, the Pristina Corps, with this reference in the last sentence, related only to actions in which there was coordinated action and support for the MUP units by the corps unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And if in any of those orders there's a reference to "engaging the armed non-Siptar population," who's going to control them? Is it the army? Is it the Joint Command? Is it the MUP?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nobody, unless it was stated in the task.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: All right. Speaking of -- of task, in this particular order, P2014, you'll see we have, I think, five -- five separate tasks to different elements of the VJ. And for each one of those units -- 5.1 is the 252nd Armoured Brigade. At the very end you'll see it says: "The forward command post shall be in Tupan Mahala village." And for each of the other four units you'll see at the end of the task there is listed a forward command post or -- or a command post for each of those subordinate units; correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. And you recall yesterday we had the discussion about the command post for the 354th in Lausa village. That was in Exhibit P1428, I believe. And you told us that really that -- elements of the Pristina Corps Command were co-located in that command post and they -- that's where the operation was going to be led from and not commanded by you; right?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But it's an action, not an operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Yes, I -- I stand corrected on that. I probably will make that mistake again. But here in this order issued by you, at the very end, in item 14, we have a provision that "Coordination between the elements of combat dispositions during the planning, organisation, and conduct of combat operations in the Drenica sector shall be carried out by the command of the 252nd Armoured Brigade, which will be in charge of the planning, organising, and conducting combat operations." So, General, the point I want to put to you is that you are very precise and know how to put that kind of thing in an order if that's what's contemplated and that's what's intended. I see Mr. Bakrac on his feet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, in this mountain of documents I cannot find this text very quickly in order to check it. It's not on the screen, and the interpreter has noted that he's looking only at the English text and cannot see the B/C/S original. So none of us can actually follow this. I don't doubt that my learned friend read correctly, but the translation might be wrong. So it would assist us to have the original version in B/C/S so that we can check whether the document says what it's translated as saying.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: That -- that should be on the screen. Are you able there when you need to to print off a hard copy of a document? No. You don't have that facility. All right. Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes. Could we then have the last page of this exhibit, P2014. And the general does have a hard copy.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Were you following along as I read, General? Did I read it correctly?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You probably read it correctly, but the interpretation I heard was not what it says here.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Do you want to read out the B/C/S version for and then -- for us and then we can hear if there's a difference?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Coordinated action between elements of the combat disposition in the course of the planning, organising, preparation, and carrying out of combat operations in the areas of Drenica shall be carried out by the command of the 252nd Armoured Brigade, which will be in charge of the planning, organising, and conducting of combat operations."

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's Correction: Combat activities, not operations.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: With -- with that last change, General, you can see why perhaps I have some confusion about referring to certain things as "operations" and -- instead of "actions." But my -- my question is: Why wasn't there such a precise indication of who was going to be commanding those operations in the document we were talking about yesterday with the 354th's command post in Lausha village?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My answer is the following: Throughout the war, to the best of my recollection, in several actions which were of a smaller scale, the corps command decided to order that one of the brigades which was closest to the area of activities be in charge of getting all the forces together in the conduct and carrying out of the task. And there are at least two or three examples of this happening. That's why the corps command here defines with greater precision that the entity in charge of these preparations will be the command of the 252nd Armoured Brigade. This is not any kind of exception or violation of the rules; it's simply a decision appropriate to the situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Were any elements of the Pristina Corps Command or from the forward command post intended to be at the 252nd command to help with that task?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Both the corps command and the forward command post were quite far away from the mountain of Drenica. And to the best of my recollection, no one was present when this task was being carried out. I mean no one from the corps command.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: But that, I think, is dealt with partly in paragraph 13. But, Mr. Hannis, the -- the question you asked, the previous question, what the -- the general has said is that the document before us, 2014, is no exception. And I thought your point was that you agreed and that it was 1966 and 1967 that were the possible exception. Has he really answered your question?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, my position was that his answers yesterday about that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Let me ask a question.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Lazarevic, the question you were asked a moment ago was: Why was this standard format of precision setting out who would be responsible for the coordination not used in the order P1966 and the amendment, P1967, which referred to Lausa, which we looked at yesterday?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Because in that specific action-- there were two actions. One was carried out, and a group from the corps command participated and was in charge of these activities.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So we're back round the circle that if -- if you can work out that the corps command are involved, then you don't need to say specifically that they will coordinate. That would be assumed in army terms. And somehow or other, as we discussed yesterday, that order, 1967, tells you that the corps command are involved. Is that the situation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, your summary is very good. Where there is no direct participation in control by the corps command, a subordinate unit is designated to be in charge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And when there is direct participation in control by the corps, then there's no indication of that in the document? Isn't that what you're saying? Because there is no indication in your amendment at 1967 --

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. In this exhibit, P2014, the 252nd has specific task for it. And at the end of that task, there is a reference to its command post; correct? Or its forward command post.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Forward command post.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And then at the end, in the last item, we had the specific language about how they're going to be in charge of the planning, organising, and conducting combat operations; right?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: There's also a reference in paragraph 13 to the --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: -- Pristina command being in Pristina.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Correct. Under the General Command and Communications paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Right, General?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: So I still don't understand, General, then how, with regard to your amendment in P1967, which needs to be read in conjunction with the original order or decision, P1966, 455-56, how there has been a change from the original provision about "The Joint Command shall command and direct all forces during combat operations." There is no annulment of that in your amendment. And you know how to do that kind of thing, don't you?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This sentence in documents of this kind has no meaning for the specific engagement of the unit, be it annulled or not annulled. It does not affect them in any way. And this is what I've said at least five times so far, but let me repeat once again, by Your Honours' leave: This is something that I spoke about yesterday. Parts of the command organs were deployed at the observation post to monitor the course of the action. I never said that any Joint Command, regardless of what it says here, directed, commanded the units of the army, and of the MUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Let me go on to another document. Can we next look at 4D097. And, General, if you will hand the usher back that hard copy that you have, I'll give you a hard copy of the one we're looking at now. Thank you. General, these are minutes of a briefing of the commanders of the Pristina Corps and the Pristina military district and organs of command of the 3rd Army at the forward command post on 7 August 1998. Have -- have you seen this document before? I think it may have been shown to you.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether this was the other day, whether this was just shown in the courtroom at one point, but this was the only time that I saw it. At that time and up until this time, I had not seen this document. I don't know whether you showed this document to me yesterday. I --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- can't really be more specific than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: No, I didn't. If -- if you need more time to look at it at any point, let me know. But we -- we see that the participants include General Samardzic, General Pavkovic, Colonel -- Colonel Djakovic. And then there's a reference to "Chief of Staff." I'm not sure who that means in the context. You know all those people; right?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And the first item under "Colonel Djakovic," it says: "We have finalised the decision on crushing the sabotage and terrorist forces in the Glodjane village area." Were you -- you were aware of that situation and that decision around the 7th of August, 1998, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not at this meeting. I was not at any of the meetings at -- of the 3rd Army forward command post. I can give you my interpretation of what it says here and what people said at this meeting, if I am allowed to do so, but at that time I was not aware of all those discussions and of who said what, because I was not present there.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, are -- are you familiar with Glodjane village?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And it -- do you know, were -- were there not joint actions between the MUP and VJ in Glodjane village area sometime shortly after the 7th of August, 1998?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that there was a counter-terrorist action in the Glodjane village sector in the direction of the Radonjic Lake.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: If you'll go down to a couple of -- one, two, three references to "commander" speaking. And one says: "Terrain clearing adopted." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Now, I know from your evidence and some of the documents we've seen is that terrain-clearing is something that you were very diligent about. And we see the bullet point says: "The Joint Command is reviewing this issue with the municipal organs." Did you not know about that, that municipal organs and the Joint Command were reviewing the issue of terrain clearing in August 1998?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not aware of what is written here, but I do know that the municipal organs are duty-bound, with their sanitation organs, to take measures to remove any noxious substances that might harm humans and the environment, and I assume that the army commander - that's he - that he speaks about the 19th Preventive Health Care Institute that should take measures to prevent infectious diseases. That's a sentence below the one that you just quoted to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Can we go -- if you can go to the next page. And we need to go to page 2 of the English. General, if you can find a reference to "Colonel Djakovic" again. And, actually, the part I'm interested in is the first comment below "Colonel Djakovic," where it refers to the acronym "NS" with a full banana over it, which I understand is an abbreviation for "Chief of Staff." Do you find that?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And who would the Chief of Staff -- who would that have been referring to in this context of a meeting at the forward command post of the 3rd Army in August of 1998?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of the Chief of Staff who was supposed to sign here on page 3 on the right-hand side. That's Lieutenant-General Miodrag Simic, who testified here.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And you'll see that first sentence after the initials for him, it says: "Given the position of the state and military leadership, the terminology we shall use is 'supporting MUP forces'." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Was that information conveyed to you that that was the terminology that should be used? And I am assuming a bit here, but I'm assuming in the context of writing orders for engagement and actions against the terrorist forces.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You asked me two questions here. The first answer is that I did not get this information. And the second, in terms of terminology, that's the language that was used in numerous orders from the army commander. And there it was defined in quite certain terms how this support is to be carried out. This evidence has already been exhibited here.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, when did you first get orders from the army commander implementing that language about supporting MUP forces?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you are referring to me as the Chief of Staff, I cannot give you a precise answer, because I did not receive from the army commander any orders. You know that. I don't want to repeat that for the umpteenth time that I was carrying out a task at the border over a period of several months, so I don't know when the Pristina Corps Command, the command of my corps, received its specific tasks. I know that in every combat report from the 3rd Army Command sent to the General Staff - and we've seen a dozen or so of those - that this phrase was used. I did not see any documents that would explain what General Simic is talking about here.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, we -- we see that language in a lot of orders about those actions, but going back to 2014, P2014 that we just looked at and that I just took your hard copy away. If I could hand it back to you. I'm sorry. But in light of your answer, I have to ask you to read item 5.1, which is on page 5 of the English.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Should I read the whole sentence, then?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Can you just read the first part up to the colon in English. I want to see if it -- my English translation is accurate.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Should I read it?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Yes.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "252nd Armoured Brigade with the detachment of the PJP and JSO from the line of deployment Gajraki-Belanice, trig point 648, Veseljevic village, Crni Lug village, Dubrava and Spagi and Rasave, unnamed hill to 1.5 kilometres south of trig point 722 shall attack along the axes of Malisevo village, Klecka village, and Lapusnik village.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you. I stop you there because you did cover the points I was curious about. It does say: "The 252nd Armoured Brigade with the PJP Detachment and the JSO shall attack." Now, in other orders I know we've seen the task of the unit is to support the MUP, which will be attacking along such-and-such a line. Here it seems to say that the VJ and those MUP units will be both attacking; isn't that correct? Isn't that how that reads?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There is a difference between those two documents in the manner of the engagement, both of the police and the army. There are differences. The difference is as follows: In the first document, the army is simply providing support; and in the second document, when the police unit was supposed to be re-subordinated to the army, then an order is issued for the army to carry out this task together with this police unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And one of the reasons for that difference is in 1999 the war is on. And in 1998, when this position was taken that the word "supporting MUP forces" should be used, there was a concern about the international community's view of how the army was being used against a civilian population in Kosovo; correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that is not correct, because in the initial period of the war up until the 20th or 25th of April, in the documents that are headed by "Joint Command," the term used is "support to the MUP forces" in the performance of certain tasks although this was a state of war. Only once the re-subordination order was issued, the term "support" is no longer used and the term, the invented term, "Joint Command" is no longer used.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go back to 4D097, if we could, please, to the point where we were. It's on page 2 of the English near the bottom. And, General, if you could find the point where we were before where General Simic was talking about "supporting MUP forces." Do you have that?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And below that, we see an entry for "Commander." "We have to make a separate plan for each segment of engagement of forces. Let's hope to God that this is how it pans out." And next it says: "In future, we will have to send the MUP precise tasks." What kinds of precise tasks would the army be sending to the MUP? In August of 1998?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please clarify whether I am now required to comment on what the army commander meant to say or actually said or to share my personal experience or my view what I know and how to interpret what is said here, because I really don't know whether the army commander actually said that. And at least of all, can I now tell you what he meant? So could you please guide me; what am I supposed to tell you?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, first of all, I guess you should tell me was there any translation problem? Is what I said, was it interpreted to you consistent with what you're reading in the document? Or was there some problem?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The interpretation I received was correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: So it -- I guess I would like you to comment on, if you know anything about what kind of precise task were sent or would have been sent to the MUP by the army in August of 1998. Anything you can tell us about that.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this regard and in light of the topic that we're discussing now, the support to the MUP forces, I can tell you, by the Honourable Trial Chamber's leave, and I can remind you that we had a very, very specific document from the 3rd Army commander in which he defines how this support is to be carried out; that some police units cannot send their support request to the units of the army, but that this should all be done at the level of the MUP leadership; and then the army commander, the corps commander, or the Chief of Staff of the army should approve that support. This is the way I read this. And I know that it was ordered at that time, so that all the requests from the police for support should be submitted in this manner and a decision was to be made in accordance with the order of the 3rd Army commander by the 3rd Army commander, by the Chief of Staff of the army, the corps commander, but not by the brigade commanders.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, General, as best I understand your answer, you're talking about a situation where the police are sending requests to the army for support. But I read this as the army sending precise task to the MUP. Do you know anything about that, about the army giving precise task to the MUP?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know of a single example when we're talking about the Pristina Corps. I take the liberty of saying that the army commander could not have ordered the police to do anything. We saw a document where he proposed to the chief of the General Staff how -- where the police should set up its check-points. And this was something that was to be solved at the level of the chief of the General Staff and the Minister of the Interior, Stojilkovic at that time. So I really don't know what this sentence as it reads, what it refers to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Lazarevic, would you go back to the word "Commander," and would you read the first sentence after the word "Commander," please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "We will have to make a separate plan for each segment of the engagement of forces. Let's hope to God that this is how it pans out."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: General --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: The reason I asked for that is I don't understand what in English "each segment of engagement of forces" means. But we've got the same translation again, so that doesn't advance the matter. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, General, you've just heard the comment by Judge Bonomy, and I share that. To you, what does that mean, "each segment of engagement of forces"? Do you know what that refers to?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm afraid that now I'm being asked -- well, I will try as much as I can with the best of intentions, but --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I don't want you to try and speculate. If you had some --

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Really, I really can't tell you. I don't know. I didn't see the document before and I wasn't there.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Fair enough. Thank you. Let's go next, then, to Exhibit P1427. General, this is a -- And I'll trade you hard copies, with the help of the usher. This is a decision by General Pavkovic on the 10th of August, 1998 on the joint engagement of MUP and VJ forces. Have you seen this one before?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember this document from the proofing sessions here. I think actually that this was shown in court on at least two occasions through several witnesses, actually.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Did you see it in 1998?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall having seen this document in 1998. And, well, here on the last page you can see that this was not sent to the forward command post. I know the situation. I know what this refers to. But we're talking about the document. The question is whether I saw this document at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes. And in item 1, where it says: "I have decided with MUP and VJ forces to smash the sabotage terrorist forces stronghold and establish control," it lists several villages in the area to be dealt with. And this includes Glodjane village that we were talking about before; right?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I think there has been a misunderstanding, because General Lazarevic seems to be waiting for a question and Mr. Hannis seems to be waiting for an answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I really didn't understand ...

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: General, I wanted to ask you if this action contemplates action in the area of Glodjane village.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you. And if you'll look at item number 6 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: If we're going to be going into this in some detail, perhaps we should stop now, break, and resume at ten minutes to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: That's fine. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: General, we were talking about Exhibit P1427. Shortly before the break I -- I brought this to your attention. And we see this is the 10th of August, 1998 and it appears to be from the Pristina Corps Command forward command post. That's where you were located in August of 1998; correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And this decision was General Pavkovic's decision, signed by him. And item number 6 says: "The combat operations will be commanded by the Joint Command for Kosovo and Metohija from the forward command post of the Pristina Corps in Djakovica." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Were you not aware of this document at the time in 1998? You were there with General Pavkovic; right?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first day when the action began, I was on the left flank of the border at Dragas, so I was not with General Pavkovic and the part of the corps command that had come to the IKM on the first day, but the action lasted for two or three days, so I came later and I know what happened later. As for the document, I'm telling you I didn't see it at that time. The corps command came to the forward command post on a number of occasions. This was not the first time.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And how did you come to be out on the left flank? Were you sent there by General Pavkovic?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. As far as I remember, one captain got killed. He was in the border guard service. And I went up there -- when I say "up there," I mean the extreme left, 100 kilometres away from Djakovica, to see what the situation was like and to stabilise the security of the border in that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: When had you left the forward command post to go to that location?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In early morning hours, as soon as we learned about the incident. It had happened the previous night, that ambush attack on the army. And I went early in the morning to inspect the location of that incident.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... the 9th of August?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm talking about the day when the action was supposed to begin, the 10th or the 11th. I believe that's when the action started.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, can you help me out? The order is dated the 10th for an action for the 11th, I believe. So which day was it you left the command post in Djakovica and which day did you return?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I left on the day when the action began and I returned that evening. But if I'm to pinpoint the date, I know it was the date when the action began. I returned the evening on -- of that day. We could see in the report. It doesn't mean that necessarily the action began that day, but whether it was really carried out then, we can't see from this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, if you left the day the action occurred, then were you not present in the command post on the day this order was written? Because it was written on the 10th, contemplating action on the 11th. So if the action took place, it either took place on the 11th or later; correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I dare say that it would be very comfortable for the commander and the Chief of Staff to spend the entire day in Djakovica in one place. Even when the commander comes, we see each other briefly and then we move on to perform the tasks. I was practically in flying mode during the action. When I say "flying," I mean on the border on a daily basis, and there was a standing team that planned and performed that action.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... were you in the command post on the 10th of August, when this order is dated -- or this decision is dated?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that. I don't know whether I was at the forward command post or I was touring a unit. All I know for a fact is that when the action began, I wasn't there. I came that evening. But the action lasted for at least one more day.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: All right. And we'll see at the end of this document where it lists the persons or the units to whom it was sent, it included the Republic of Serbia MUP PJP command." Correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what is written in the addressees list.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And in the task for units, under item 2.1, we have Battle Group 52 supporting the attack that's launched by certain MUP elements. Item 2.2 is BG-549-3 supporting some MUP elements. Item 2.4 is worded slightly differently, and it says: "Battle Group 125-3, in coordinated action with the MUP, attacks" along a certain axis. What's the difference in the significance of that wording between "in coordinated action with," as opposed to "supports"? Can you explain that for us?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'll try. There is certainly a distinction in tactical and technical terms and in practical terms. When we talk about "support," then a certain army unit follows the combat disposition of the police unit. It is authorised to support MUP forces by its manoeuvre, disposition, movement and fire; whereas, "coordinated action" is a general relationship in which everyone performs their own task, taking care to avoid friendly fire, and the MUP unit has its own unit -- has its own tasks. The army units on the left and on the right have their own tasks. But the purpose of coordinated action is primarily to avoid friendly fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... 2.5 is even further slightly differently worded. It says: "BG-15.3 with the 7th MUP Od attacks." Now, I assume -- is that -- is that just sloppy writing? Because it doesn't say "in coordinated action with"; it simply says"with." I assume it's not supposed to be in uncoordinated action with.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I understand what is written here as a technical error, maybe a typographical error. I understand that in paragraph 2.4 it should have been written -- there is also some handwriting there, but I don't know whether it refers to that paragraph. I see that in my hard copy, but I see something on the screen as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, in regard to these -- these joint actions and -- and the role between the army and the MUP, I want to ask you about another document from May 1999, after the war is on. First of all, you know who Colonel Milan Kotur was; correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: What was -- what was his position in the Pristina Corps in May of 1999?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Chief of the infantry organ of the Pristina Corps Command.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And who was your Chief of Staff in May of 1999?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Colonel Veroljub Zivkovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Can you clarify for me what kinds of authority could be delegated by you to your Chief of Staff. For example, if there was an operation or an action being planned against the terrorist forces, could -- could your Chief of Staff write that order and sign it?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the Chief of Staff can write an order for an anti-terrorist activity and engagement, previously informing and obtaining consent from me, and on the basis of my prior order; or alternatively, if there was a sudden attack, then he could take measures independently. And let me remind the Honourable Trial Chamber that in the examination-in-chief there was a Defence exhibit introduced whereby one of my orders formed special forces and I made the Chief of Staff responsible for using them in -- on the route of Kosare and preventing the breakthrough of forces from Albania. That is an answer to your question how all this is regulated and defined.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And could your Chief of Staff further delegate that authority?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Chief of Staff, being in charge of the forward command post, has a deputy when he is absent, and that deputy takes care of the functioning of the forward command post and the discharging of its functions. This delegation, as you call it, can be understood that way too, but the gist is that there is a deputy of the person who is in charge of the forward command post who performs the duties of the Chief of Staff whenever the Chief of Staff is unable to perform this duty.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Within the competence of Colonel Kotur, as chief of the infantry organ of the Pristina Corps Command, was he permitted to write these kind of orders to crush the Siptar terrorist forces? Could that be delegated to him by either you or the Chief of Staff?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not particularly deal with the -- the powers Colonel Kotur had or anybody else at the forward command post. I knew more about the Chief of Staff. It was within the powers of the Chief of Staff to order that somebody from the corps command stand in for him in his absence, and that including Colonel Kotur.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: You're saying that at that stage and with your subsequent army experience you can't tell us whether the chief of the infantry of the Pristina Corps could, in appropriate circumstances, write this kind of order?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He was able to on the authorisation from the Chief of Staff. That's what I said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Sorry. Yes. I didn't pick up the last sentence. It's my mistake. Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: General, I'd next like to look at Exhibit P2011. And I can hand you a hard copy and make a trade with you again. Thank you. General, this is from the command of the Pristina Corps forward command post dated the 20th of May, 1999. And it's an order to crush the Siptar terrorist forces in the Radonjicko Jezero sector. And it -- in English, it's translated as "Operation Sekac." Could you read the Serbian for me. Should it be translated as "Action Sekac"?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Akcija Sekac is written, action.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Have you -- have you seen this document before?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have seen the document during proofing.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And you'll see on the -- on the last page that it's signed by Colonel Kotur.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see that it's written: "On the authority of the Chief of Staff, Colonel Milan Kotur," and his signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Now, in this operation, it -- which apparently is -- "readiness for attack" is described as the last thing under item number 4 on page 4 of the English. "Readiness for attack at 0500 hours on 22" -- which apparently has been scratched out, and then -- "23 May, 1999." And you'll see "Tasks of units." The first one is for the 122nd MUP Detachment of a strength of three PJP companies shall in the first phase launch an attack along a certain axis. And item 5.2 on the next page in English is for the 3rd MUP Detachment to search and mop up terrain. And item number 5.3 is the 4th Company of the 124th MUP Brigade to mop up terrain, et cetera. There are a couple more of these, I think, where this order from the VJ is directing MUP units to attack and carry out parts of this Action Sekac. Did you know that? Did you know that was going on?, that the VJ was ordering the MUP units?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was in keeping with the orders of the President of the State, the Supreme Command Staff, the army command, and my order on the re-subordination of MUP to the army. And in that context, it is certain that it was in keeping with all that at the time we are talking about.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: So do you know if this operation proceed as -- as planned on the 23rd of May, 1999? I'm sorry, this action.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that this action lasted practically until the end of the war, involving great problems and losses, and that after this action, which was unsuccessful, there was another action by the corps command -- or rather, signed by the corps command from the forward command post, signed by the Chief of Staff of the corps, to lift the siege of police forces. It was a specific situation where the police found themselves encircled by strong forces of armed insurgency in the sector of Radonjicko Jezero, Jablanica, and the Chief of Staff took measures to lift that siege from the MUP unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Did you, prior to writing your 24th of May, 1999 report about the failure of the MUP to be subordinated, did you have any information or complaint from Colonel Kotur or the Chief of Staff at the forward command post that MUP was not following the order for subordination?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it was common knowledge that nowhere, not a single area of Kosovo and Metohija, were MUP units able to accept decision-making or orders from army units, because they were not authorised to do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, my question is: As -- as a matter of fact, was there any indication that there was a problem in this particular operation on the part of MUP in following the order from Colonel Kotur? Did the 4th Company of the 124th MUP Brigade refuse to follow the order that applied to them, or the 73rd MUP Detachment, et cetera? Did you have any indication that there was a problem in this specific action?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Concerning this particular action, I cannot provide any details, but I know for a fact and I assert that Colonel Stefanovic at that time went on a number of occasions to Djakovica and together with the Chief of the Secretariat of the Interior, together with the forward command post of the corps, he tried to solve the problem of resubordination and to maintain coordination and cooperation. But I am talking about the entire period of the war. You are asking me about this specific thing, but I am -- I think this applies to this case as well. I know that he went to Djakovica to solve that problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, when -- when did he go to Djakovica to solve the problem?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I think that by the time this action began -- and I remember it had stages 1 and 2, although we don't see it from this document. We can see it from some other reports, involving great losses on both sides. I mean the army and the police. Precisely because of the problem of insufficient coordination and failure to re-subordinate. I cannot say whether it was the 20th May or the 23rd or the 25th, but I'm certain that when General Radojko Stefanovic comes to testify, he will come to assist us all and he will be able to answer this specific question.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Let me move to another topic. I'd like to show you Exhibit P1439. I'll hand you a hard copy and trade you. General, this is a Pristina Corps Command document dated the 5th of October, 1998 to the 3rd Army Command. It's from General Pavkovic. Have you seen this one before?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I have not seen it before -- I had not seen it before proofing. I believe it has been shown in the courtroom previously once or twice.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And you'll see in item number 1 Pavkovic is advising his superior, General Samardzic, that "Contrary to your orders, Pristina Corps Command has not formed any new BG," combat groups. And in item number 2, he mentions that "The plan to smash the sabotage forces on the territory of Kosovo and Metohija, authorised by the President of the FRY, stipulated that when sabotage forces had been smashed by the MUP and the VJ, rapid-intervention forces shall be formed to be at full readiness, with the engagement of helicopters," et cetera. Did you know about this plan to form rapid-intervention forces? Did you know about that in October 1998?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Later on I learned about this initiative. I didn't know about it at the time. As the forces had been withdrawn, both army and police forces, at the state level it was decided from the battalion of the corps and from parts of the MUP to have, if there is an attack by terrorist forces on the terrorist -- by the terrorist forces on the MUP and army. I learned about this later on, and these were very small-scale forces, up to company level, but actually they were never formed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And you don't recall this matter being discussed in your presence at any time in 1998?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From this document, you can see where this happened. It happened in Pristina. I wish to remind everybody that I was away from Pristina and I didn't hear these conversations or follow this correspondence. Later on I learnt that there was even a decision issued by the President of the State but that it was not carried through.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Is this not a subject that General Pavkovic would have discussed with you, as his Chief of Staff?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, he couldn't discuss it with me on the telephone and he wouldn't come to Djakovica personally for that reason. As I can see, he talked about this at a meeting in Belgrade attended by the army commander, the corps commander, and the President of the State. I was not included in this not because I wasn't trusted but because this concerned a very small force, at platoon or company level, with one helicopter. So I don't think the corps commander needed to include me in that at the time, given that it was such a small unit they were discussing.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: You just said in that answer something about a meeting in Belgrade. "As I can see, he talked about this at a meeting in Belgrade." Where do you draw that inference from? I don't see a reference to a meeting in Belgrade. I see that -- go ahead.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: By your leave, in item 2, the last sentence, after that comma: "As ordered by the President," it says. I think that the President issued this order to them at one of the meetings, because I never had occasion to see a written order in the corps command saying that it had arrived from the President of the Republic concerning the forming of an intervention unit. I know that the army commander and the corps commander used to go to see the chief of the General Staff and that on several occasions they visited the President of the Republic. So that's what I base my conclusion on, and on what it says here.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Well, in item 2 it does say that rapid-intervention force -- forces were to be formed, as ordered by the President. It's not clear to me from reading this when that order was given and how it was given, whether it was in person or by phone or in writing. But the -- the next paragraph under "2" says: "On my return from the reporting session with the ZK" -- and here it's translated with a question mark as "Joint Commission."
